title: Microsoft Purview DLP: stop Copilot grounding on external emails
summary: Hold: the displayed PowerShell command creates a policy but does not configure the external-email exclusion, and the UI path skips creating a rule. The claim that licensing is unpublished also overlooks Microsoft's published licensing table for restricting Copilot processing of files and emails.

claims.claim: This roadmap item concerns Microsoft Purview.
Microsoft describes this as a real-time DLP control for external email.
claims.quote: This real-time control helps organizations mitigate data risks by preventing Microsoft 365 Copilot and Chat from processing emails from senders external to your organization.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: When enabled, the control excludes external senders' emails from Copilot grounding.
claims.quote: When the policy detects that an email was received from a sender outside your organization's accepted domains, Copilot excludes that email from grounding, summarization, and citation.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Excluded external emails are not referenced or cited in responses.
claims.quote: When the policy detects that an email was received from a sender outside your organization's accepted domains, Copilot excludes that email from grounding, summarization, and citation.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Excluded external emails are omitted from Copilot summaries.
claims.quote: When a user prompts Copilot to summarize their inbox or reason over recent email, external emails are excluded from grounding.

claims.claim: Copilot continues using permitted internal Microsoft 365 sources.
claims.quote: Copilot continues to use internal Microsoft 365 data sources where permitted, and the user's access to the email itself isn't affected.

claims.where: front matter: licensing; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because Microsoft has not published a licence requirement for this control.
claims.quote: | Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to restrict Copilot from processing files and emails | Not included | Not included | Not included | Included | Included |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to per-user. Replace the blanket unpublished-licensing statements, including the cost rationale and licensing open question, with: 'Microsoft publishes licensing for DLP that restricts Copilot processing of files and emails: it is included with Microsoft 365 E5/A5, Office 365 E5/A5 and the Purview suite and Information Protection and Governance plans listed in the service description, but not with the listed Business or E3 plans. The external-email preview article names no separate SKU.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description#microsoft-purview-data-loss-prevention-dlp-for-microsoft-copilot. Replace 'The only cost the sources show is admin time' with 'Check whether existing licences cover the published DLP entitlement; policy creation, testing and communication also take admin time.'

claims.claim: The condition follows directly after selecting the Copilot location in the displayed policy-creation path.
claims.quote:
On the **Locations** page, set the **Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork** location to on.
5. Add a rule with the **Content contains** > **Sensitive information types** condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.
claims.fix: Do not present the condition as a child of the location. Narrow controls[0].ui.path and the rendered table to the documented wizard path: 'Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork'. Replace the row note's UI qualification with: 'Preview. After selecting the location, add a rule with Email is received from > External users and the action Prevent Copilot from processing content; these are rule settings, not navigation beneath the location.' This path and these rule settings are documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name "<policy name>" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences") implements the external-email exclusion.
claims.quote: The fourth command creates the DLP policy using the `$loc` variable for the value of the Locations parameter, and "Copilot Policy" as the name of the policy (use any unique name).
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null and render that side as Not yet documented. The named cmdlet and parameters exist, but this call only creates a policy container and does not add the external-sender condition or blocking action. Replace the automation note with: 'The policy-creation cmdlet is documented, but the external-email rule's PowerShell syntax is not documented in the references checked in November 2026.' Searches for Copilot external email PowerShell and New-DlpComplianceRule external email sender returned no documented Copilot rule call; New-DlpComplianceRule documents FromScope only for policies scoped to Exchange.
